newsitem.title: UK: Port operators criticised over bulk loading speeds.
newsitem.headline: Port operators criticised over bulk loading speeds.

text.p: Increasing bulk terminal loading speeds have been criticised by the International Association of Dry Cargo Shipowners (Intercargo).
Intercargo Chairman Sverre Tidemand said today the "interface between ship and shore is vital" in the search for improved bulk carrier safety.
Tidemand said: "Loading rates of 16,000 tonnes per hour are being reached at some ports. Ballast systems can't cope with this speed of loading."
He added that Intercargo was investigating the extent of the problem round the world with shipowners compiling reports into terminal loading experiences.
Terminal operators dispute the levels claimed by owners and claim that rates are varied by cargo, ship size and condition.
However, Tidemand said: "We get reports from masters that do not match statements by port operators that there is no problem over loading." -- Paul Berrill, Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087
